summary: A 1922-23 Blaw-Knox lookout in the Allegheny National Forest's Hearts Content area that reported a 1923 wildfire; its access today is unverified.

facts.design: Blaw-Knox tower with 7x7 ft metal cab and sloping legs below the last four sections

events.note: Cooperative tower plans announced; the first plans called for a wooden tower
Construction announced for September 1922; concrete base reported finished in October
Register gives 1923 as the year built
Wheeler lookout reported the Farnsworth Fire on May 20, 1923
Andrew Marfink of Cherry Grove announced as the Wheeler lookout (March 22, 1924 item)

evidence.supports: tower located in Hearts Content Recreation Area; one of first tracts acquired for the forest in 1923
evidence.quote: The tower is located in the Hearts Content Recreation Area, an area designated as a National Natural Landmark, that was one of the first tracts acquired for Allegheny National Forest upon its founding in 1923.

evidence.supports: location in Allegheny National Forest, Warren County, Pennsylvania
evidence.quote: Allegheny National Forest Warren County, Pennsylvania

evidence.supports: built 1923; sloping legs below last four vertical sections
evidence.quote: Built in 1923, the tower has sloping legs until the last four sections which are vertical.

evidence.supports: Blaw-Knox design with 7x7 metal cab; described in present tense
evidence.quote: The Wheeler Fire Tower on the Allegheny National Forest is an unusual Blaw-Knox tower with 7’x7’ metal cab.

evidence.supports: April 1, 1921 item: plans for cooperative tower with the state forestry department
evidence.quote: The tower will be built and manned under a co-operative agreement between Wheeler & Dusenbury, and the state department of forestry.

evidence.supports: first plans called for a wooden tower
evidence.quote: Plans are being laid for a wooden forest fire tower.

evidence.supports: October 26, 1922 item: concrete base finished, steel to arrive the next week
evidence.quote: Work on the new fire tower on Wheeler and Dusenbury lands is going forward rapidly and the concrete base has been completed ready to put up the steel which will arrive next week.

evidence.supports: September 5, 1922 item: construction announced for an 80 foot tower, Limestone township
evidence.quote: Construction work will start Tuesday Morning on the erection of an 80 foot fire tower on Wheeler and Dusenbury lands in Limestone township in this county.

evidence.supports: planned 80 feet and highest in state
evidence.quote: The tower will be the highest in the state and will be 80 feet from base to the top.

evidence.supports: hut on top with ranger on duty in fire season
evidence.quote: On the top will be a hut with a ranger constantly on duty during the fire season.
The state forestry department of Pennsylvania has begun the erection of the first fire tower to be placed in Warren county, which will be placed on the Wheeler & Dusenbury farm in Watson township.

evidence.supports: March 22, 1924 item: Andrew Marfink to be stationed in Wheeler tower
evidence.quote: Andrew Marfink, of Cherry Grove, will be stationed in the forest lookout tower at Wheeler.

evidence.supports: Farnsworth Fire of May 20, 1923 reported by the Wheeler lookout; over 1000 acres
evidence.quote: The Farnsworth fire was estimated to be over 1000 acres and started on May 20th, 1923, when it was reported by the Wheeler Lookout Tower at 2:45 pm.

evidence.supports: company gave 20 acres of virgin forest now Hearts Content Scenic Area
evidence.quote: Wheeler & Dusenbury donated the 20-acre virgin forest that is now a Natural Landmark known as Hearts Content Scenic Area to the Forest Service.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers show construction announced for September 1922 and steel due in autumn 1922; the register gives 1923, and a May 1923 fire report shows the lookout in use that year
A 1921 plan called for a wooden tower; 1922 reports describe steel arriving for the tower
Two 1922 newspaper items name different townships for the same tower (Limestone and Watson)

sources.title: This Month in History on the Allegheny
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Allegheny National Forest

notes_for_editor: Height is left out of facts. Newspapers gave 80 feet (1922); the record's 27.4 m (90 ft) comes from the PA ArcGIS storymap, which could not be read as text, so it is not quoted. A WebFetch summary of Waymarking gave 1922, 80 feet and a locked fence at the base, but no verbatim quote could be checked, so it is not cited. No source found on access today, and no staffing after 1924. The 2009 register is the newest source. The Facebook post about the 1923 fire was not used.
